You are an expert code reviewer specializing in modern software development across multiple languages and frameworks. Your primary responsibility is to review code against project guidelines in CLAUDE.md with high precision to minimize false positives.

By default, review unstaged changes from `git diff`. The user may specify different files or scope to review.

Identify the specific unproved requirement before requesting more work; missing required evidence cannot pass. Acceptance must wait until all required tests have passing evidence, even when the task is not in the Blocked lane. An allowed retry permits remediation, not acceptance or dependent phase advancement. Inspect supporting contracts as needed without reopening the full implementation chain or adding acceptance requirements.
- **Phase:** in the same dispatch as the task reviews, assess the complete phase requirements and cross-task behavior. Use the task verdicts and evidence; conclude READY TO ADVANCE or BLOCKED with the unmet requirement or dependency.
- **Final:** follow the assigned `impl-review` domain and criteria.

Each blocking finding must identify the violated AC, defined test or existing mandatory constraint, concrete evidence, and the smallest correction. Severity alone does not expand the assignment. Optional hardening belongs in follow-ups.

Return a consolidated finding set within that contract. Route unrelated findings separately; they block only when they prevent the current contract from being met or make acceptance unsafe under an existing requirement. These boundaries govern the responsibilities below.

In a phase review, return a separate AC/test verdict for each task alongside the phase verdict; the tasks stay In Review until the review clears. Remain read-only. On re-review, assess only the affected tasks and preserve unaffected evidence.

## Core Review Responsibilities

**Project Guidelines Compliance**: Verify adherence to explicit project rules (typically in CLAUDE.md or equivalent) including import patterns, framework conventions, language-specific style, function declarations, error handling, logging, testing practices, platform compatibility, and naming conventions.

**Bug Detection**: Identify actual bugs that will impact functionality - logic errors, null/undefined handling, race conditions, memory leaks, security vulnerabilities, and performance problems.

**Code Quality**: Evaluate significant issues like code duplication, missing critical error handling, accessibility problems, and inadequate test coverage.

## Confidence Scoring

Rate each potential issue on a scale from 0-100:

- **0**: Not confident at all. This is a false positive that doesn't stand up to scrutiny, or is a pre-existing issue.
- **25**: Somewhat confident. This might be a real issue, but may also be a false positive. If stylistic, it wasn't explicitly called out in project guidelines.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to read

offset.description: The line number to start reading from. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once

limit.description: The number of lines to read. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once.

pages.description: Page range for PDF files (e.g., "1-5", "3", "10-20"). Only applicable to PDF files. Maximum 20 pages per request.

allow_large.description: Set to true to read a text file, or a line range of one, that is over the usual size limits, up to what still fits in your context. Only use this when you genuinely need all of it or the user asked for the whole file; otherwise read it in parts with offset and limit, or search it.

tools.name: WebFetch
tools.description:
Fetches a URL, converts the page to markdown, and answers `prompt` against it using a small fast model.

- Fails on authenticated/private URLs — use an authenticated MCP tool or `gh` for those instead.
- Fails on localhost and other hostnames without a dot; for a local server, use curl via Bash.
- HTTP is upgraded to HTTPS. Cross-host redirects are returned to you rather than followed; call again with the redirect URL.
- Responses are cached for 15 minutes per URL.

url.description: The URL to fetch content from

prompt.description: The prompt to run on the fetched content

offset.description: Character position in the page text to start reading from. Use it to read on through a page too long for one call, with the value the previous result gave.

tools.name: TaskStop
tools.description:
- Stops a running background task by its ID
- Takes a task_id parameter identifying the task to stop
- To stop an agent-team teammate, pass its agent ID or bare teammate name as task_id
- To stop a background agent spawned with a name, pass that name as task_id
- Returns a success or failure status
- Use this tool when you need to terminate a long-running task

task_id.description: The ID of the background task to stop. Agent-team teammates and named background agents are also accepted by agent ID or name.

tools.name: Glob
tools.description: Fast file pattern matching. Supports glob patterns like "**/*.js" or "src/**/*.ts". Returns matching file paths sorted by modification time.

pattern.description: The glob pattern to match files against

path.description: The directory to search in. If not specified, the current working directory will be used. IMPORTANT: Omit this field to use the default directory. DO NOT enter "undefined" or "null" - simply omit it for the default behavior. Must be a valid directory path if provided.

tools.name: Grep
tools.description:
Content search built on ripgrep. Prefer this over `grep`/`rg` via Bash — results integrate with the permission UI and file links.

- Full regex syntax (e.g. "log.*Error", "function\s+\w+"). Ripgrep, not grep — escape literal braces (`interface\{\}`).
- Filter with `glob` (e.g. "**/*.tsx") or `type` (e.g. "js", "py", "rust").
- `output_mode`: "content" (matching lines), "files_with_matches" (paths only, default), or "count".
- `multiline: true` for patterns that span lines.

pattern.description: The regular expression pattern to search for in file contents

path.description: File or directory to search in (rg PATH). Defaults to current working directory.

glob.description: Glob pattern to filter files (e.g. "*.js", "*.{ts,tsx}") - maps to rg --glob

output_mode.description: Output mode: "content" shows matching lines (supports -A/-B/-C context, -n line numbers, head_limit), "files_with_matches" shows file paths (supports head_limit), "count" shows match counts (supports head_limit). Defaults to "files_with_matches".

-B.description: Number of lines to show before each match (rg -B). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-A.description: Number of lines to show after each match (rg -A). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (rg -C). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-n.description: Show line numbers in output (rg -n). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to true.

-o.description: Print only the matched (non-empty) parts of each matching line, one match per output line (rg -o / --only-matching). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to false.

type.description: File type to search (rg --type). Common types: js, py, rust, go, java, etc. More efficient than include for standard file types.

head_limit.description: Limit output to first N lines/entries, equivalent to "| head -N". Works across all output modes: content (limits output lines), files_with_matches (limits file paths), count (limits count entries). Defaults to 250 when unspecified. Pass 0 for unlimited (use sparingly — large result sets waste context).

offset.description: Skip first N lines/entries before applying head_limit, equivalent to "| tail -n +N | head -N". Works across all output modes. Defaults to 0.

multiline.description: Enable multiline mode where . matches newlines and patterns can span lines (rg -U --multiline-dotall). Default: false.

- Do NOT Write report/summary/findings/analysis .md files. Return findings directly as your final assistant message — the parent agent reads your text output, not files you create. (Files written as input to another tool are fine; this note is about report files.)

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.name: WebFetch
tools.description:
Fetches a URL, converts the page to markdown, and answers `prompt` against it using a small fast model.

- Fails on authenticated/private URLs — use an authenticated MCP tool or `gh` for those instead.
- Fails on localhost and other hostnames without a dot; for a local server, use curl via Bash.
- HTTP is upgraded to HTTPS. Cross-host redirects are returned to you rather than followed; call again with the redirect URL.
- Responses are cached for 15 minutes per URL.

pattern.description: The regular expression pattern to search for in file contents

path.description: File or directory to search in (rg PATH). Defaults to current working directory.

glob.description: Glob pattern to filter files (e.g. "*.js", "*.{ts,tsx}") - maps to rg --glob

output_mode.description: Output mode: "content" shows matching lines (supports -A/-B/-C context, -n line numbers, head_limit), "files_with_matches" shows file paths (supports head_limit), "count" shows match counts (supports head_limit). Defaults to "files_with_matches".

-B.description: Number of lines to show before each match (rg -B). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-A.description: Number of lines to show after each match (rg -A). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (rg -C). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-n.description: Show line numbers in output (rg -n). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to true.

-o.description: Print only the matched (non-empty) parts of each matching line, one match per output line (rg -o / --only-matching). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to false.

type.description: File type to search (rg --type). Common types: js, py, rust, go, java, etc. More efficient than include for standard file types.

head_limit.description: Limit output to first N lines/entries, equivalent to "| head -N". Works across all output modes: content (limits output lines), files_with_matches (limits file paths), count (limits count entries). Defaults to 250 when unspecified. Pass 0 for unlimited (use sparingly — large result sets waste context).

offset.description: Skip first N lines/entries before applying head_limit, equivalent to "| tail -n +N | head -N". Works across all output modes. Defaults to 0.

multiline.description: Enable multiline mode where . matches newlines and patterns can span lines (rg -U --multiline-dotall). Default: false.

1	"""The shared public query result shape."""
2	
3	from __future__ import annotations
4	
5	from dataclasses import dataclass
6	
7	
8	@dataclass(frozen=True)
9	class Result:
10	    columns: list[str]
11	    types: list[str]
12	    rows: list[tuple]
13	
14	
15	def parse_integer(text: str) -> int:
16	    """Convert validated, optionally signed ASCII decimal digits in chunks."""
17	    negative = text.startswith("-")
18	    if text[:1] in ("+", "-"):
19	        text = text[1:]
20	    value = int(text[:9])
21	    for start in range(9, len(text), 9):
22	        chunk = text[start:start + 9]
23	        value = value * 10 ** len(chunk) + int(chunk)
24	    return -value if negative else value
25	
26	
27	def integer_text(value: int) -> str:
28	    """Render an arbitrary-size integer without unbounded decimal conversion."""
29	    sign = "-" if value < 0 else ""
30	    value = abs(value)
31	    chunks = []
32	    while value >= 1_000_000_000:
33	        value, chunk = divmod(value, 1_000_000_000)
34	        chunks.append(str(chunk).zfill(9))
35	    chunks.append(str(value))
36	    return sign + "".join(reversed(chunks))
37

1	"""Handwritten SQL lexer with code-point offsets and LF-only positions."""
2	
3	from __future__ import annotations
4	
5	from dataclasses import dataclass
6	import re
7	
8	from .errors import LexError
9	from .model import parse_integer
10	
11	
12	KEYWORDS = frozenset(
13	    "SELECT DISTINCT FROM WHERE GROUP BY HAVING ORDER ASC DESC LIMIT OFFSET "
14	    "AS JOIN INNER LEFT OUTER ON AND OR NOT IS NULL LIKE ESCAPE IN".split()
15	)
16	_NAME = re.compile(r"[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*")
17	_NUMBER = re.compile(
18	    r"(?:[0-9]+\.[0-9]*|\.[0-9]+)(?:[eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?"
19	    r"|[0-9]+[eE][+-]?[0-9]+|[0-9]+"
20	)
21	_NUMBER_CONTINUATION = re.compile(r"[A-Za-z0-9_.]")
22	
23	
24	@dataclass(frozen=True)
25	class Token:
26	    kind: str
27	    raw: str
28	    value: str | int | float | None
29	    start: int
30	    end: int
31	    line: int
32	    column: int
33	
34	
35	def tokenize(sql: str) -> list[Token]:
36	    """Tokenize the entire source, including a positioned terminal EOF token.
37	
38	    Kinds are INT, REAL, STRING, IDENT, QUOTED_IDENT, EOF, uppercase reserved
39	    keywords, or the operator/punctuation itself. Offsets are zero-based and
40	    end-exclusive; line/column are one-based. Values decode quotes/numbers;
41	    keyword values are uppercase and EOF's value is None.
42	    """
43	    tokens = []
44	    i, line, column = 0, 1, 1
45	
46	    def advance(end: int) -> None:
47	        nonlocal i, line, column
48	        text = sql[i:end]
49	        newlines = text.count("\n")
50	        if newlines:
51	            line += newlines
52	            column = len(text.rsplit("\n", 1)[1]) + 1
53	        else:
54	            column += end - i
55	        i = end
56	
57	    while i < len(sql):
58	        char = sql[i]
59	        if char in " \t\r\n":
60	            advance(i + 1)
61	            continue
62	        if sql.startswith("--", i):
63	            end = sql.find("\n", i)
64	            advance(len(sql) if end == -1 else end)
65	            continue
66	
67	        start, token_line, token_column = i, line, column
68	        if char in "\"'":
69	            quote = char
70	            end = i + 1
71	            decoded = []
72	            while end < len(sql):
73	                if sql[end] == quote:
74	                    if end + 1 < len(sql) and sql[end + 1] == quote:
75	                        decoded.append(quote)
76	                        end += 2
77	                        continue
78	                    end += 1
79	                    break
80	                decoded.append(sql[end])
81	                end += 1
82	            else:
83	                description = ("string literal" if quote == "'"
84	                               else "quoted identifier")
85	                raise LexError(f"unterminated {description}", line, column)
86	            kind = "STRING" if quote == "'" else "QUOTED_IDENT"
87	            value = "".join(decoded)
88	        elif "0" <= char <= "9" or (
89	            char == "." and i + 1 < len(sql) and "0" <= sql[i + 1] <= "9"
90	        ):
91	            match = _NUMBER.match(sql, i)
92	            end = match.end()
93	            if end < len(sql) and _NUMBER_CONTINUATION.fullmatch(sql[end]):
94	                raise LexError("invalid number literal", line, column)
95	            raw = match.group()
96	            kind = "REAL" if any(c in raw for c in ".eE") else "INT"
97	            value = float(raw) if kind == "REAL" else parse_integer(raw)
98	        elif match := _NAME.match(sql, i):
99	            end = match.end()
100	            raw = match.group()
101	            kind = raw.upper() if raw.upper() in KEYWORDS else "IDENT"
102	            value = raw if kind == "IDENT" else kind
103	        elif sql[i:i + 2] in ("<>", "!=", "<=", ">="):
104	            end = i + 2
105	            kind = value = sql[i:end]
106	        elif char in "+-*/%=<>(),.;":

3	from __future__ import annotations
4	
5	import csv
6	from dataclasses import dataclass
7	from os import PathLike, fspath
8	from pathlib import Path
9	import re
10	
11	from .errors import DataIOError, SemanticError
12	from .model import parse_integer
13	
14	
15	_INTEGER = re.compile(r"[+-]?[0-9]+")
16	_REAL = re.compile(r"[+-]?([0-9]+\.[0-9]*|\.[0-9]+|[0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?")
17	
18	
19	@dataclass(frozen=True)
20	class Table:
21	    name: str
22	    columns: list[str]
23	    types: list[str]
24	    rows: list[tuple]
25	
26	
27	class Catalog:
28	    def __init__(self, data_dir: str | PathLike[str]) -> None:
29	        directory = fspath(data_dir)
30	        self._path = Path(directory)
31	        try:
32	            if not self._path.is_dir():
33	                raise DataIOError(f"data directory not found: {directory}")
34	        except OSError as error:
35	            raise DataIOError(f"{self._path.name}: {error.strerror}") from error
36	
37	    def _files(self) -> list[Path]:
38	        try:
39	            return [path for path in self._path.iterdir()
40	                    if path.name.lower().endswith(".csv") and path.is_file()]
41	        except OSError as error:
42	            raise DataIOError(f"{self._path.name}: {error.strerror}") from error
43	
44	    def tables(self) -> list[str]:
45	        return sorted((path.name[:-4] for path in self._files()),
46	                      key=lambda name: (name.lower(), name))
47	
48	    def load(self, name: str, line: int = 1, column: int = 1) -> Table:
49	        matches = [path for path in self._files()
50	                   if path.name[:-4].lower() == name.lower()]
51	        if not matches:
52	            raise SemanticError(f"unknown table '{name}'", line, column)
53	        if len(matches) > 1:
54	            raise DataIOError(f"ambiguous table file '{name}'")
55	        path = matches[0]
56	        columns = None
57	        raw_rows = []
58	        try:
59	            with path.open(encoding="utf-8-sig", newline="") as stream:
60	                reader = csv.reader(stream, strict=True)
61	                try:
62	                    for fields in reader:
63	                        if not fields:
64	                            continue
65	                        if columns is None:
66	                            columns = fields
67	                            seen = set()
68	                            for header in columns:
69	                                if not header:
70	                                    raise DataIOError(f"{path.name}: empty column name")
71	                                if header.lower() in seen:
72	                                    raise DataIOError(
73	                                        f"{path.name}: duplicate column '{header}'")
74	                                seen.add(header.lower())
75	                        elif len(fields) != len(columns):
76	                            raise DataIOError(
77	                                f"{path.name}: line {reader.line_num}: expected "
78	                                f"{len(columns)} fields, got {len(fields)}")
79	                        else:
80	                            raw_rows.append(fields)
81	                except csv.Error as error:
82	                    raise DataIOError(
83	                        f"{path.name}: line {reader.line_num}: malformed CSV") from error
84	        except UnicodeDecodeError as error:
85	            raise DataIOError(f"{path.name}: invalid UTF-8") from error
86	        except OSError as error:
87	            raise DataIOError(f"{path.name}: {error.strerror}") from error
88	        if columns is None:
89	            raise DataIOError(f"{path.name}: empty file")
90	
91	        types = []
92	        for index in range(len(columns)):
93	            fields = [row[index] for row in raw_rows if row[index] != ""]
94	            if fields and all(_INTEGER.fullmatch(field) for field in fields):
95	                types.append("INTEGER")
96	            elif fields and all(_REAL.fullmatch(field) for field in fields):
97	                types.append("REAL")
98	            else:
99	                types.append("TEXT")
100	        converters = {"INTEGER": parse_integer, "REAL": float, "TEXT": str}
101	        rows = [tuple(None if field == "" else converters[kind](field)
102	                      for field, kind in zip(row, types)) for row in raw_rows]
103	        return Table(path.name[:-4], columns, types, rows)
104	
105	    def schema(self, name: str) -> list[tuple[str, str]]:
106	        table = self.load(name)
107	        return list(zip(table.columns, table.types))

1	"""Pure, deterministic CSV and aligned-table output."""
2	
3	from __future__ import annotations
4	
5	from .model import Result, integer_text
6	
7	
8	def _value_text(value: int | float | str) -> str:
9	    if isinstance(value, int):
10	        return integer_text(value)
11	    return repr(value) if isinstance(value, float) else str(value)
12	
13	
14	def _csv_field(value: int | float | str | None) -> str:
15	    if value is None:
16	        return ""
17	    text = _value_text(value)
18	    if (
19	        not text
20	        or any(char in text for char in ',"\r\n')
21	        or text.startswith(" ")
22	        or text.endswith(" ")
23	    ):
24	        return '"' + text.replace('"', '""') + '"'
25	    return text
26	
27	
28	def format_csv(result: Result) -> str:
29	    """Return LF-terminated CSV, distinguishing NULL from empty TEXT."""
30	    lines = [",".join(_csv_field(name) for name in result.columns)]
31	    lines.extend(
32	        ",".join(_csv_field(value) for value in row) for row in result.rows
33	    )
34	    return "\n".join(lines) + "\n"
35	
36	
37	def _table_cell(value: int | float | str | None) -> str:
38	    text = "NULL" if value is None else _value_text(value)
39	    return text.replace("\r", "\\r").replace("\n", "\\n")
40	
41	
42	def format_table(result: Result) -> str:
43	    """Return an escaped, code-point-aligned table with a row-count footer."""
44	    headers = [_table_cell(name) for name in result.columns]
45	    rows = [[_table_cell(value) for value in row] for row in result.rows]
46	    widths = [len(header) for header in headers]
47	    for row in rows:
48	        for index, cell in enumerate(row):
49	            widths[index] = max(widths[index], len(cell))
50	
51	    lines = [" | ".join(cell.ljust(width) for cell, width in zip(headers, widths))]
52	    lines.append("-+-".join("-" * width for width in widths))
53	    for values, cells in zip(result.rows, rows):
54	        lines.append(" | ".join(
55	            cell.rjust(width) if isinstance(value, (int, float)) else cell.ljust(width)
56	            for value, cell, width in zip(values, cells, widths)
57	        ))
58	    count = len(result.rows)
59	    lines.append(f"({count} {'row' if count == 1 else 'rows'})")
60	    return "\n".join(line.rstrip(" ") for line in lines) + "\n"

15	def parse_integer(text: str) -> int:
16	    """Convert validated, optionally signed ASCII decimal digits in chunks."""
17	    negative = text.startswith("-")
18	    if text[:1] in ("+", "-"):
19	        text = text[1:]
20	    value = int(text[:9])
21	    for start in range(9, len(text), 9):
22	        chunk = text[start:start + 9]
23	        value = value * 10 ** len(chunk) + int(chunk)
24	    return -value if negative else value
25	
26	
27	def integer_text(value: int) -> str:
28	    """Render an arbitrary-size integer without unbounded decimal conversion."""
29	    sign = "-" if value < 0 else ""
30	    value = abs(value)
31	    chunks = []
32	    while value >= 1_000_000_000:
33	        value, chunk = divmod(value, 1_000_000_000)
34	        chunks.append(str(chunk).zfill(9))
35	    chunks.append(str(value))
36	    return sign + "".join(reversed(chunks))

1	"""Handwritten SQL lexer with code-point offsets and LF-only positions."""
2	
3	from __future__ import annotations
4	
5	from dataclasses import dataclass
6	import re
7	
8	from .errors import LexError
9	from .model import parse_integer
10	
11	
12	KEYWORDS = frozenset(
13	    "SELECT DISTINCT FROM WHERE GROUP BY HAVING ORDER ASC DESC LIMIT OFFSET "
14	    "AS JOIN INNER LEFT OUTER ON AND OR NOT IS NULL LIKE ESCAPE IN".split()
15	)
16	_NAME = re.compile(r"[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*")
17	_NUMBER = re.compile(
18	    r"(?:[0-9]+\.[0-9]*|\.[0-9]+)(?:[eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?"
19	    r"|[0-9]+[eE][+-]?[0-9]+|[0-9]+"
20	)
21	_NUMBER_CONTINUATION = re.compile(r"[A-Za-z0-9_.]")
22	
23	
24	@dataclass(frozen=True)
25	class Token:
26	    kind: str
27	    raw: str
28	    value: str | int | float | None
29	    start: int
30	    end: int
31	    line: int
32	    column: int
33	
34	
35	def tokenize(sql: str) -> list[Token]:
36	    """Tokenize the entire source, including a positioned terminal EOF token.
37	
38	    Kinds are INT, REAL, STRING, IDENT, QUOTED_IDENT, EOF, uppercase reserved
39	    keywords, or the operator/punctuation itself. Offsets are zero-based and
40	    end-exclusive; line/column are one-based. Values decode quotes/numbers;
41	    keyword values are uppercase and EOF's value is None.
42	    """
43	    tokens = []
44	    i, line, column = 0, 1, 1
45	
46	    def advance(end: int) -> None:
47	        nonlocal i, line, column
48	        text = sql[i:end]
49	        newlines = text.count("\n")
50	        if newlines:
51	            line += newlines
52	            column = len(text.rsplit("\n", 1)[1]) + 1
53	        else:
54	            column += end - i
55	        i = end
56	
57	    while i < len(sql):
58	        char = sql[i]
59	        if char in " \t\r\n":
60	            advance(i + 1)
61	            continue
62	        if sql.startswith("--", i):
63	            end = sql.find("\n", i)
64	            advance(len(sql) if end == -1 else end)
65	            continue
66	
67	        start, token_line, token_column = i, line, column
68	        if char in "\"'":
69	            quote = char
70	            end = i + 1
71	            decoded = []
72	            while end < len(sql):
73	                if sql[end] == quote:
74	                    if end + 1 < len(sql) and sql[end + 1] == quote:
75	                        decoded.append(quote)
76	                        end += 2
77	                        continue
78	                    end += 1
79	                    break
80	                decoded.append(sql[end])
81	                end += 1
82	            else:
83	                description = ("string literal" if quote == "'"
84	                               else "quoted identifier")
85	                raise LexError(f"unterminated {description}", line, column)
86	            kind = "STRING" if quote == "'" else "QUOTED_IDENT"
87	            value = "".join(decoded)
88	        elif "0" <= char <= "9" or (
89	            char == "." and i + 1 < len(sql) and "0" <= sql[i + 1] <= "9"
90	        ):
91	            match = _NUMBER.match(sql, i)
92	            end = match.end()
93	            if end < len(sql) and _NUMBER_CONTINUATION.fullmatch(sql[end]):
94	                raise LexError("invalid number literal", line, column)
95	            raw = match.group()
96	            kind = "REAL" if any(c in raw for c in ".eE") else "INT"
97	            value = float(raw) if kind == "REAL" else parse_integer(raw)
98	        elif match := _NAME.match(sql, i):
99	            end = match.end()
100	            raw = match.group()
101	            kind = raw.upper() if raw.upper() in KEYWORDS else "IDENT"
102	            value = raw if kind == "IDENT" else kind
103	        elif sql[i:i + 2] in ("<>", "!=", "<=", ">="):
104	            end = i + 2
105	            kind = value = sql[i:end]
106	        elif char in "+-*/%=<>(),.;":
107	            end = i + 1
108	            kind = value = char
109	        else:
110	            raise LexError(f"unexpected character '{char}'", line, column)
111	        tokens.append(Token(kind, sql[start:end], value, start, end,
112	                            token_line, token_column))
113	        advance(end)
114	
115	    tokens.append(Token("EOF", "", None, i, i, line, column))
116	    return tokens
117

87	            raise DataIOError(f"{path.name}: {error.strerror}") from error
88	        if columns is None:
89	            raise DataIOError(f"{path.name}: empty file")
90	
91	        types = []
92	        for index in range(len(columns)):
93	            fields = [row[index] for row in raw_rows if row[index] != ""]
94	            if fields and all(_INTEGER.fullmatch(field) for field in fields):
95	                types.append("INTEGER")
96	            elif fields and all(_REAL.fullmatch(field) for field in fields):
97	                types.append("REAL")
98	            else:
99	                types.append("TEXT")
100	        converters = {"INTEGER": parse_integer, "REAL": float, "TEXT": str}
101	        rows = [tuple(None if field == "" else converters[kind](field)
102	                      for field, kind in zip(row, types)) for row in raw_rows]
103	        return Table(path.name[:-4], columns, types, rows)
104	
105	    def schema(self, name: str) -> list[tuple[str, str]]:
106	        table = self.load(name)
107	        return list(zip(table.columns, table.types))

1	"""Pure, deterministic CSV and aligned-table output."""
2	
3	from __future__ import annotations
4	
5	from .model import Result, integer_text
6	
7	
8	def _value_text(value: int | float | str) -> str:
9	    if isinstance(value, int):
10	        return integer_text(value)
11	    return repr(value) if isinstance(value, float) else str(value)
12	
13	
14	def _csv_field(value: int | float | str | None) -> str:
15	    if value is None:
16	        return ""
17	    text = _value_text(value)
18	    if (
19	        not text
20	        or any(char in text for char in ',"\r\n')
21	        or text.startswith(" ")
22	        or text.endswith(" ")
23	    ):
24	        return '"' + text.replace('"', '""') + '"'
25	    return text
26	
27	
28	def format_csv(result: Result) -> str:
29	    """Return LF-terminated CSV, distinguishing NULL from empty TEXT."""
30	    lines = [",".join(_csv_field(name) for name in result.columns)]
31	    lines.extend(
32	        ",".join(_csv_field(value) for value in row) for row in result.rows
33	    )
34	    return "\n".join(lines) + "\n"
35	
36	
37	def _table_cell(value: int | float | str | None) -> str:
38	    text = "NULL" if value is None else _value_text(value)
39	    return text.replace("\r", "\\r").replace("\n", "\\n")
40	
41	
42	def format_table(result: Result) -> str:
43	    """Return an escaped, code-point-aligned table with a row-count footer."""
44	    headers = [_table_cell(name) for name in result.columns]
45	    rows = [[_table_cell(value) for value in row] for row in result.rows]
46	    widths = [len(header) for header in headers]
47	    for row in rows:
48	        for index, cell in enumerate(row):
49	            widths[index] = max(widths[index], len(cell))
50	
51	    lines = [" | ".join(cell.ljust(width) for cell, width in zip(headers, widths))]
52	    lines.append("-+-".join("-" * width for width in widths))
53	    for values, cells in zip(result.rows, rows):
54	        lines.append(" | ".join(
55	            cell.rjust(width) if isinstance(value, (int, float)) else cell.ljust(width)
56	            for value, cell, width in zip(values, cells, widths)
57	        ))
58	    count = len(result.rows)
59	    lines.append(f"({count} {'row' if count == 1 else 'rows'})")
60	    return "\n".join(line.rstrip(" ") for line in lines) + "\n"

13	## Lexer protocol
14	
15	`from minisql.lexer import Token, tokenize`; `tokenize(sql: str) -> list[Token]` lexes the whole string, including a terminal EOF token. `KEYWORDS` is the exact reserved set, a frozenset of uppercase strings; aggregate function names remain ordinary identifiers.
16	
17	`Token` is a frozen dataclass with fields, in order:
18	
19	| Field | Meaning |
20	|---|---|
21	| kind | `INT`, `REAL`, `STRING`, `IDENT`, `QUOTED_IDENT`, `EOF`, an uppercase keyword, or the operator/punctuation itself |
22	| raw | Exact token source spelling, including any quotes |
23	| value | int/float for numbers; decoded str for names/strings; uppercase str for keywords; raw symbol for punctuation; None for EOF |
24	| start, end | Zero-based code-point offsets, end-exclusive |
25	| line, column | One-based token-start coordinates; only LF splits lines |
26	
27	In particular, a NULL token is a keyword token whose value is `"NULL"`; consumers derive the NULL literal's type/value from its kind, not from token.value. `007` decodes to int 7, `1e2` to float 100.0. Quoted names retain their case in decoded value; resolution later uses lower(), not casefold(). Unicode is accepted inside quotes, not in unquoted ASCII identifiers or numbers. Numeric continuation checking is ASCII as specified in feature-specification.md §5.2. Comments end only at LF. EOF has raw `""`, value None, start=end=len(sql), and the position immediately after all input, including trailing whitespace/comments.
28	
29	## Parser entry and ownership boundary
30	
31	`from minisql.parser import parse`; `parse(sql: str) -> minisql.ast.Query` fully tokenizes before constructing the parser, so LexError anywhere in the input precedes a possible ParseError. No catalog, name/function resolution, static typing, execution, or output formatting occurs here. For example, unknown function names, non-COUNT star calls, and multi-character literal ESCAPEs parse and await semantic validation.
32	
33	All AST records are frozen dataclasses, with inherited `start: int, end: int` fields first. Spans are code-point offsets into `Query.source`, end-exclusive. All sequence fields below are tuples. Optional tokens/nodes use None. All name/alias/operator/star/ESCAPE fields below are original lexer Token objects, not rewritten strings.
34	
35	### Expressions (`minisql.ast.Expr` subclasses)
36	
37	- `Literal(start, end, token)`: INT/REAL/STRING/NULL; token.kind preserves static literal kind and token.value preserves decoded numeric/string values.
38	- `Column(start, end, name, qualifier)`: name Token and optional qualifier Token. A qualified reference starts at its qualifier. Both IDENT and QUOTED_IDENT are accepted.
39	- `Unary(start, end, operator, operand)`: unary +/- or prefix NOT. The operator is its exact token.
40	- `Binary(start, end, left, operator, right)`: arithmetic, comparisons, AND, OR. Keyword operator kinds are uppercase, raw spelling remains unchanged; != and <> remain distinct.
41	- `IsNull(start, end, operand, operator, not_token, null_token)`: operator is IS, optional not_token is NOT.
42	- `Like(start, end, operand, operator, pattern, not_token, escape_keyword, escape)`: operator is LIKE even for NOT LIKE; escape_keyword is ESCAPE and escape is its STRING token. Runtime LIKE errors belong at operator; invalid ESCAPE length belongs at escape.
43	- `In(start, end, operand, operator, items, not_token, lparen, rparen)`: operator is IN even for NOT IN; items is a nonempty tuple of full expressions.
44	- `Call(start, end, name, argument, star, lparen, rparen)`: exactly one of argument Expr or star Token is present. Name is an ordinary or quoted name token. COUNT(*)'s star position is available directly.
45	- `Parenthesized(start, end, expression, lparen, rparen)`: explicit wrapper, including nested wrappers, with its own outer span. Parentheses are not erased during parsing.
46	
47	Precedence is unary signs > multiplicative > additive > one comparison/predicate > recursive NOT > left-associative AND > left-associative OR. Comparisons cannot chain without explicit parentheses; failure is at the second operator. Calls take one expression or star; IN has at least one expression. LIMIT/OFFSET take INT tokens, never signed, real, or parenthesized expressions.
48	
49	### Query and surrounding records
50	
51	- `Wildcard(start, end, star, qualifier)`: a Node, not an Expr; star Token and optional qualifier Token for bare * or q.*. Only projection items accept it.
52	- `SelectItem(start, end, expression, alias, as_token)`: expression is Expr or Wildcard; alias and as_token are optional name/AS tokens. Explicit AS and implicit aliases remain distinguishable. A SelectItem span includes its alias when present, while its expression span never includes that alias. Wildcards have no alias production.
53	- `TableRef(start, end, name, alias, as_token)`: name/alias Tokens; effective range name is alias if present, else name. TableRef span includes its alias.
54	- `Join(start, end, kind, table, condition, keyword, join_token, outer_token, on_token)`: kind is `INNER` for JOIN/INNER JOIN, `LEFT` for LEFT [OUTER] JOIN. keyword is the first JOIN/INNER/LEFT token; join_token is JOIN; outer_token exists only for LEFT OUTER JOIN; on_token is ON. condition is a complete Expr.
55	- `OrderItem(start, end, expression, direction)`: optional ASC/DESC Token; None means ASC. Span includes a direction if present; expression span does not.
56	- `Query(start, end, source, select_token, distinct, items, from_table, joins, where, group_by, having, order_by, limit, offset, semicolon)`: source is the entire original sql string. distinct is its DISTINCT Token or None. items is a nonempty SelectItem tuple. from_table is optional; joins are in source order. where/having are optional expressions. group_by and order_by are tuples, empty when absent. limit/offset are optional unsigned INT Tokens; use `.value` for the integer. semicolon is its optional token. 5	## Shared imports available to parallel tasks
6	
7	- `from minisql.errors import MiniSQLError, LexError, ParseError, SemanticError, QueryRuntimeError, DataIOError`
8	- All accept `(message, line=None, column=None)`, including keyword arguments. `.message`, `.line`, `.column`, `.kind` are available; exception `.args` contains the message. Class-specific kinds are `Lex`, `Parse`, `Semantic`, `Runtime`, `IO`. DataIOError always has None positions, even if positions are supplied.
9	- SQL error strings are `<Kind>Error at line L, column C: <message>`; data errors are `IOError: <message>`. No newline is added by the classes.
10	- `from minisql.model import Result`: frozen dataclass with `columns: list[str]`, `types: list[str]`, `rows: list[tuple]`, in that constructor order. Freezing prevents field reassignment, not mutation of the contract-required lists. It does not coerce or validate caller-provided values.
11	- Initial `minisql.__init__` reexports exactly those errors and Result. It does not import catalog, formatting, parser, or future engine/CLI modules. T4 owns final public integration.
12	
13	## Lexer protocol
14	
15	`from minisql.lexer import Token, tokenize`; `tokenize(sql: str) -> list[Token]` lexes the whole string, including a terminal EOF token. `KEYWORDS` is the exact reserved set, a frozenset of uppercase strings; aggregate function names remain ordinary identifiers.
16	
17	`Token` is a frozen dataclass with fields, in order:
18	
19	| Field | Meaning |
20	|---|---|
21	| kind | `INT`, `REAL`, `STRING`, `IDENT`, `QUOTED_IDENT`, `EOF`, an uppercase keyword, or the operator/punctuation itself |
22	| raw | Exact token source spelling, including any quotes |
23	| value | int/float for numbers; decoded str for names/strings; uppercase str for keywords; raw symbol for punctuation; None for EOF |
24	| start, end | Zero-based code-point offsets, end-exclusive |
25	| line, column | One-based token-start coordinates; only LF splits lines |
26	
27	In particular, a NULL token is a keyword token whose value is `"NULL"`; consumers derive the NULL literal's type/value from its kind, not from token.value. `007` decodes to int 7, `1e2` to float 100.0. Quoted names retain their case in decoded value; resolution later uses lower(), not casefold(). Unicode is accepted inside quotes, not in unquoted ASCII identifiers or numbers. Numeric continuation checking is ASCII as specified in feature-specification.md §5.2. Comments end only at LF. EOF has raw `""`, value None, start=end=len(sql), and the position immediately after all input, including trailing whitespace/comments.
28	
29	## Parser entry and ownership boundary
30	
31	`from minisql.parser import parse`; `parse(sql: str) -> minisql.ast.Query` fully tokenizes before constructing the parser, so LexError anywhere in the input precedes a possible ParseError. No catalog, name/function resolution, static typing, execution, or output formatting occurs here. For example, unknown function names, non-COUNT star calls, and multi-character literal ESCAPEs parse and await semantic validation.
32	
33	All AST records are frozen dataclasses, with inherited `start: int, end: int` fields first. Spans are code-point offsets into `Query.source`, end-exclusive. All sequence fields below are tuples. Optional tokens/nodes use None. All name/alias/operator/star/ESCAPE fields below are original lexer Token objects, not rewritten strings.
34	
35	### Expressions (`minisql.ast.Expr` subclasses)
36	
37	- `Literal(start, end, token)`: INT/REAL/STRING/NULL; token.kind preserves static literal kind and token.value preserves decoded numeric/string values.
38	- `Column(start, end, name, qualifier)`: name Token and optional qualifier Token. A qualified reference starts at its qualifier. Both IDENT and QUOTED_IDENT are accepted.
39	- `Unary(start, end, operator, operand)`: unary +/- or prefix NOT. The operator is its exact token.
40	- `Binary(start, end, left, operator, right)`: arithmetic, comparisons, AND, OR. Keyword operator kinds are uppercase, raw spelling remains unchanged; != and <> remain distinct.
41	- `IsNull(start, end, operand, operator, not_token, null_token)`: operator is IS, optional not_token is NOT.
42	- `Like(start, end, operand, operator, pattern, not_token, escape_keyword, escape)`: operator is LIKE even for NOT LIKE; escape_keyword is ESCAPE and escape is its STRING token. Runtime LIKE errors belong at operator; invalid ESCAPE length belongs at escape.
43	- `In(start, end, operand, operator, items, not_token, lparen, rparen)`: operator is IN even for NOT IN; items is a nonempty tuple of full expressions.
44	- `Call(start, end, name, argument, star, lparen, rparen)`: exactly one of argument Expr or star Token is present. Name is an ordinary or quoted name token. COUNT(*)'s star position is available directly.
45	- `Parenthesized(start, end, expression, lparen, rparen)`: explicit wrapper, including nested wrappers, with its own outer span. Parentheses are not erased during parsing.
46	
47	Precedence is unary signs > multiplicative > additive > one comparison/predicate > recursive NOT > left-associative AND > left-associative OR. Comparisons cannot chain without explicit parentheses; failure is at the second operator. Calls take one expression or star; IN has at least one expression. LIMIT/OFFSET take INT tokens, never signed, real, or parenthesized expressions.
48	
49	### Query and surrounding records
50	
51	- `Wildcard(start, end, star, qualifier)`: a Node, not an Expr; star Token and optional qualifier Token for bare * or q.*. Only projection items accept it.
52	- `SelectItem(start, end, expression, alias, as_token)`: expression is Expr or Wildcard; alias and as_token are optional name/AS tokens. Explicit AS and implicit aliases remain distinguishable. A SelectItem span includes its alias when present, while its expression span never includes that alias. Wildcards have no alias production.
53	- `TableRef(start, end, name, alias, as_token)`: name/alias Tokens; effective range name is alias if present, else name. TableRef span includes its alias.
54	- `Join(start, end, kind, table, condition, keyword, join_token, outer_token, on_token)`: kind is `INNER` for JOIN/INNER JOIN, `LEFT` for LEFT [OUTER] JOIN. keyword is the first JOIN/INNER/LEFT token; join_token is JOIN; outer_token exists only for LEFT OUTER JOIN; on_token is ON. condition is a complete Expr.
55	- `OrderItem(start, end, expression, direction)`: optional ASC/DESC Token; None means ASC. Span includes a direction if present; expression span does not.
56	- `Query(start, end, source, select_token, distinct, items, from_table, joins, where, group_by, having, order_by, limit, offset, semicolon)`: source is the entire original sql string. distinct is its DISTINCT Token or None. items is a nonempty SelectItem tuple. from_table is optional; joins are in source order. where/having are optional expressions. group_by and order_by are tuples, empty when absent. limit/offset are optional unsigned INT Tokens; use `.value` for the integer. semicolon is its optional token. Query span runs from SELECT through the last syntactic token, including a semicolon when present but excluding trailing comments/whitespace. EOF consumes all remaining input; only one semicolon is accepted.

61	2. Unparenthesized column: only a direct `isinstance(item.expression, ast.Column)` qualifies for its resolved CSV header. Parenthesized(Column) does not qualify.
62	3. Otherwise derive heading by `query.source[item.expression.start:item.expression.end]`. This retains case, spaces, comments, multiline strings, and parentheses without including aliases or surrounding whitespace.
63	4. Bare ORDER ordinal: expression must be a direct Literal with `token.kind == "INT"`. Parenthesized(1), unary +1, and REAL 1.0 are not bare ordinals.
64	5. Bare ORDER alias candidate: expression must be a direct Column with qualifier None. Parenthesized names and qualified names are ordinary input expressions.
65	6. For resolved structural identity, unwrap Parenthesized recursively; ignore spans/token spelling; preserve literal kind plus decoded value, operator kind/symbol identity, operand order, and resolved column identities. Do not conflate != and <> or use the heading as a structural key. This normalization belongs to T4, not the parser.

105	### Type inference
106	
107	For each column, over its non-empty raw fields (no trimming): if every field fully matches `[+-]?[0-9]+` the column is INTEGER (`int(field)`); else if every field fully matches `[+-]?([0-9]+\.[0-9]*|\.[0-9]+|[0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?` it is REAL (`float(field)`); else TEXT (fields kept verbatim, including numeric-looking ones). A column with no non-empty fields is TEXT. Empty fields (quoted or not) are NULL in every type. Consequently `" 1"` makes a column TEXT, `007` is INTEGER `7`, and `1`, `2.5` makes a REAL column.

109	## Interface contract
110	
111	### Data directory
112	
113	- `--data DIR` (default `.`); library `connect(DIR)`. A missing or non-directory `DIR` is an IOError: `connect(DIR)` raises `DataIOError` immediately, and the one-shot CLI reports it and exits 3 before lexing the SQL.
114	- A table is any regular file directly in `DIR` whose name ends in `.csv` (case-insensitive). Table name = file stem; lookup is case-insensitive. Two files whose stems are equal case-insensitively make every reference to that name an IOError `ambiguous table file '<name>'`.
115	- Files are read on each `execute` with `encoding='utf-8-sig'`, `newline=''` and `csv.reader(f, strict=True)` (default dialect). Only the tables referenced in `FROM`/`JOIN` are read; any other file in `DIR`, however malformed, never affects a query. `tables()` lists stems without reading file contents.
116	- Row 1 is the header; names are used verbatim. Empty header name, or duplicate names (case-insensitive), is an IOError. Lines yielding zero fields are skipped. A record with a different field count than the header is IOError `<file>: line N: expected K fields, got M`, where N is the reader's `line_num` after that record.
117	
118	### Name resolution and output names
119	
120	- Column reference `c` searches all tables in `FROM`; `q.c` searches the table whose range name (alias, else table name) is `q`. Zero matches: unknown column; more than one: ambiguous column. Duplicate range names are a SemanticError. An `ON` condition sees only tables introduced before or in its own join; later tables are unknown there. Joins associate left.
121	- `*` expands to all columns of all tables in `FROM` order; `t.*` to that table's columns. Duplicate output names are allowed.
122	- Output name: the alias as written (quotes removed); else for an unparenthesized column reference, the column's header name as in the CSV; else the verbatim source text of the item from its first to last character (e.g. `COUNT(*)`, `a + 1`, `(a)`).

145	### Library API
146	
147	```python
148	minisql.connect(data_dir: str | os.PathLike) -> Connection
149	Connection.execute(sql: str) -> Result
150	Connection.tables() -> list[str]                    # stems, sorted by (lower(), name)
151	Connection.schema(table: str) -> list[tuple[str, str]]  # (column, type) in header order
152	@dataclass(frozen=True)
153	class Result: columns: list[str]; types: list[str]; rows: list[tuple]
154	minisql.format_csv(result: Result) -> str
155	minisql.format_table(result: Result) -> str
156	```
157	
158	`types` holds `"INTEGER"`, `"REAL"`, `"TEXT"` or `"NULL"`. Row values are `int`, `float`, `str` or `None`.
159	
160	### Output formats
161	
162	Value text: INTEGER `str(v)`; REAL `repr(v)` (`100.0`, `2.5`, `1e+20`); TEXT verbatim.
163	
164	**CSV** (`--format csv`, default for one-shot): header line, then one line per row, fields joined by `,`, every line terminated by `\n` (also on Windows). NULL is an empty unquoted field. A field is wrapped in `"` (inner `"` doubled) iff it is the empty string, contains `,`, `"`, `\n` or `\r`, or starts or ends with a space. Header names follow the same quoting.
165	
166	**Table** (`--format table`, default for REPL): cell text is the value text with newline and carriage-return characters replaced by the two-character escapes `\n` and `\r`; NULL is `NULL`. Width of a column = max code-point length of header and cells. Header cells left-aligned; INTEGER/REAL values right-aligned; TEXT and `NULL` left-aligned. Cells joined by ` | `; separator line is `-` × width per column joined by `-+-`; trailing spaces stripped from every line; then `(N rows)` or `(1 row)`. Every line ends with `\n`.

105	### Type inference
106	
107	For each column, over its non-empty raw fields (no trimming): if every field fully matches `[+-]?[0-9]+` the column is INTEGER (`int(field)`); else if every field fully matches `[+-]?([0-9]+\.[0-9]*|\.[0-9]+|[0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?` it is REAL (`float(field)`); else TEXT (fields kept verbatim, including numeric-looking ones). A column with no non-empty fields is TEXT. Empty fields (quoted or not) are NULL in every type. Consequently `" 1"` makes a column TEXT, `007` is INTEGER `7`, and `1`, `2.5` makes a REAL column.
108	
109	## Interface contract
110	
111	### Data directory
112	
113	- `--data DIR` (default `.`); library `connect(DIR)`. A missing or non-directory `DIR` is an IOError: `connect(DIR)` raises `DataIOError` immediately, and the one-shot CLI reports it and exits 3 before lexing the SQL.
114	- A table is any regular file directly in `DIR` whose name ends in `.csv` (case-insensitive). Table name = file stem; lookup is case-insensitive. Two files whose stems are equal case-insensitively make every reference to that name an IOError `ambiguous table file '<name>'`.
115	- Files are read on each `execute` with `encoding='utf-8-sig'`, `newline=''` and `csv.reader(f, strict=True)` (default dialect). Only the tables referenced in `FROM`/`JOIN` are read; any other file in `DIR`, however malformed, never affects a query. `tables()` lists stems without reading file contents.
116	- Row 1 is the header; names are used verbatim. Empty header name, or duplicate names (case-insensitive), is an IOError. Lines yielding zero fields are skipped. A record with a different field count than the header is IOError `<file>: line N: expected K fields, got M`, where N is the reader's `line_num` after that record.
117	
118	### Name resolution and output names
119	
120	- Column reference `c` searches all tables in `FROM`; `q.c` searches the table whose range name (alias, else table name) is `q`. Zero matches: unknown column; more than one: ambiguous column. Duplicate range names are a SemanticError. An `ON` condition sees only tables introduced before or in its own join; later tables are unknown there. Joins associate left.
121	- `*` expands to all columns of all tables in `FROM` order; `t.*` to that table's columns. Duplicate output names are allowed.
122	- Output name: the alias as written (quotes removed); else for an unparenthesized column reference, the column's header name as in the CSV; else the verbatim source text of the item from its first to last character (e.g. `COUNT(*)`, `a + 1`, `(a)`).

145	### Library API
146	
147	```python
148	minisql.connect(data_dir: str | os.PathLike) -> Connection
149	Connection.execute(sql: str) -> Result
150	Connection.tables() -> list[str]                    # stems, sorted by (lower(), name)
151	Connection.schema(table: str) -> list[tuple[str, str]]  # (column, type) in header order
152	@dataclass(frozen=True)
153	class Result: columns: list[str]; types: list[str]; rows: list[tuple]
154	minisql.format_csv(result: Result) -> str
155	minisql.format_table(result: Result) -> str
156	```
157	
158	`types` holds `"INTEGER"`, `"REAL"`, `"TEXT"` or `"NULL"`. Row values are `int`, `float`, `str` or `None`.
159	
160	### Output formats
161	
162	Value text: INTEGER `str(v)`; REAL `repr(v)` (`100.0`, `2.5`, `1e+20`); TEXT verbatim.
163	
164	**CSV** (`--format csv`, default for one-shot): header line, then one line per row, fields joined by `,`, every line terminated by `\n` (also on Windows). NULL is an empty unquoted field. A field is wrapped in `"` (inner `"` doubled) iff it is the empty string, contains `,`, `"`, `\n` or `\r`, or starts or ends with a space. Header names follow the same quoting.
165	
166	**Table** (`--format table`, default for REPL): cell text is the value text with newline and carriage-return characters replaced by the two-character escapes `\n` and `\r`; NULL is `NULL`. Width of a column = max code-point length of header and cells. Header cells left-aligned; INTEGER/REAL values right-aligned; TEXT and `NULL` left-aligned. Cells joined by ` | `; separator line is `-` × width per column joined by `-+-`; trailing spaces stripped from every line; then `(N rows)` or `(1 row)`. Every line ends with `\n`.

Reviewed the F1 decimal-conversion correction, relevant regressions, task correction notes and validation evidence. **T1 PASS · T2 PASS · T3 PASS**

### Updated task verdicts

| Task | Reopened ACs | Unaffected ACs | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| **T1 — Language foundation** | **AC2 PASS:** guarded lexer regressions verify >4,300-digit integers, leading zeros, all-zero input, exact values and token positions. **AC3 PASS:** guarded parser regressions verify large literals, unary minus, parentheses, ORDER BY, LIMIT and OFFSET with retained source metadata. | **AC1, AC4, AC5, AC6 remain PASS**, reusing prior evidence; the complete defined suite also passed again. | **PASS** |
| **T2 — CSV catalog** | **AC4 PASS:** six regressions verify 5,000-digit positive, negative and explicit-plus integers, leading-zero variants and signed zero; INTEGER inference, exact values and empty-field NULL behavior are asserted. | **AC1, AC2, AC3, AC5, AC6 remain PASS**, reusing prior evidence and the passing complete catalog suite/import audit. | **PASS** |
| **T3 — Deterministic formatting** | **AC1 PASS:** complete CSV/UTF-8 goldens cover 5,001-digit positive/negative integers and zero. **AC2 PASS:** complete table goldens verify width, alignment, separator, footer and LF. **AC3 PASS:** huge-value cases verify returned strings, repeatability and unchanged Result fields/streams. | **AC4, AC5 remain PASS**, reusing prior evidence and the passing complete formatting suite. | **PASS** |

### F1 resolution and cross-task behavior

**F1 is resolved.** The [shared helpers](/Users/gkhoo-c/.Projects/mxc-c0/work/eval-c3-minisql-20261104T104418Z/minisql/model.py#L15) parse at most nine decimal digits per conversion and render only base-1,000,000,000 chunks. Sign handling, zero, leading zeros and zero-filled interior chunks are covered by the [bounded-helper tests](/Users/gkhoo-c/.Projects/mxc-c0/work/eval-c3-minisql-20261104T104418Z/tests/test_errors.py#L77).

The [lexer](/Users/gkhoo-c/.Projects/mxc-c0/work/eval-c3-minisql-20261104T104418Z/minisql/lexer.py#L97) and [catalog](/Users/gkhoo-c/.Projects/mxc-c0/work/eval-c3-minisql-20261104T104418Z/minisql/catalog.py#L100) consume `parse_integer`; both [formatters](/Users/gkhoo-c/.Projects/mxc-c0/work/eval-c3-minisql-20261104T104418Z/minisql/formatting.py#L8) consume `integer_text`. No process-global conversion setting is changed. Existing validation, REAL/TEXT/NULL handling and error paths remain unchanged.
